A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FuseUNet work and contain 17 complete, readable pages, including Appendices A–E. Text comparison and visual inspection support comparison of all equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original FuseUNet segmentation experiments and ablations in Section 4, with computational measurements, fold results, statistical analysis and visualizations in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the original FuseUNet experiments, ablations and appendix results reported in v2.

M1.justification: Section 3, Algorithm 1 and Appendix A retain the same adaptive multistep predictor-corrector fusion using nmODEs. No architecture, component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use ACDC, KiTS2023, MSD brain tumor and ISIC2017/2018 for the same 3D and 2D segmentation tasks (Table 2).

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within each comparison in Tables 3–4, including nn-UNet for ACDC/KiTS, UNETR for MSD and UltraLight VM-UNet for ISIC.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains the same five-fold 3D evaluation, 2D metrics and ablation settings. Dataset sample counts and Appendix B learning rates also match.

E4.justification: The fusion-order and memory-capacity ablations (Figure 5; Tables 5 and 11), computational-cost analysis and segmentation case studies are unchanged, including appendix visualizations.

E5.justification: Both retain fold-level reporting in Table 10 and the same standard-deviation, standard-error, confidence-interval and t-test reporting in Table 12. No run-count or seed disclosures change.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match. For example, Table 3 retains FuseUNet average Dice values of 91.57, 86.19 and 72.6 for ACDC, KiTS and MSD. The July 2025 factor-of-ten FLOPs caveat already appears in v2 and is unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorems 3.1–3.2 and A.1–A.7, Equations 1–19, and the computational-cost formulas in Table 8 retain the same mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about numerical-integration-based feature fusion, applicability across U-Net backbones and parameter reduction while preserving performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of segmentation behavior, computational tradeoffs and memory capacity are unchanged. The conclusion retains the limitation concerning historical-state storage and high memory consumption.

D1.justification: Both provide the same RTX 4090 hardware disclosure, implementation description, learning rates, memory/runtime measurements and code-access link. The repository-correction disclosure on page 9 is also retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list contain the same cited works and positioning relative to earlier U-Net and neural ODE approaches.

P1.justification: v3 adds 'Work done prior to joining University of Maryland' to the first-page affiliation footnote and adds affiliation-separating commas. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; scientific prose and document organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–9 and Tables 1–12 retain their content, captions, structure and placement. The affiliation edit fits within the existing footnote block without changing the surrounding page layout.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies an affiliation timing detail but leaves the scientific content, evidence, reproducibility information and limitations unchanged. All appendix material and the FLOPs correction note were already present in v2, so the revision produces no meaningful overall quality difference.
